hero.heading:
Looking, understanding
and remembering.
hero.description: To guide the visitor’s gaze to the artwork, so that the visitor absorbs it and takes more away from the museum.

intro.title:
More content.
More layers.
intro.body: Museums add layers to strengthen the experience: headphones, apps, AR. But every layer takes a share of the ~30 seconds a visitor gives an artwork. Absorption comes less from more information than from the quality of looking.
intro.quote: I want museum success to be measured not by how much information is shown, but by what the visitor takes away from the artwork.
intro.caption: Starting point: from Future Museums research to TRACE IV.

research.title: A short window for looking
research.finding: An artwork gets ~30 seconds of looking on average; this has barely changed since 2001.
research.decision: Design for one ~30 s moment; keep any intervention short.

research.title: Capturing and remembering
research.finding: Photographing the whole object reduces memory; zooming in on a detail does not.
research.decision: Encourage active, detail-focused looking instead of passive capture.

research.title: Zero setup at the door
research.finding: App use is low: download and pairing are barriers (vendor claim: ≤10% of visitors).
research.decision: Zero setup at the door: no download, pairing or typing numbers.

prototypes.title: Fit and refinement
prototypes.text: After researching existing eyewear temple designs, exploring users’ perceptions of hygiene, and testing physical prototypes on different people, I developed my final prototype. The design wraps more securely around the ear without creating a sense of unhygienic contact, while staying true to the Precision Organic design language established in my moodboard.

developments.title: What about users who wear glasses?
developments.text: TRACE IV envisions a removable prescription layer that adapts its transparent monocular lens to individual visual needs, enabling a more inclusive museum experience without compromising its lightweight, single-sided design.

sections.title: Option 1
sections.text: I designed a dedicated channel to accommodate interchangeable optical lenses.

sections.title: Option 2 — Hydrotac stick-on lenses
sections.text: Removable optical lenses that adhere directly to the transparent lens surface without permanent adhesives.

sections.title: Advantages
items: Easy to apply, remove, and reposition.

sections.title: Limitations
items: Potential interference with AR clarity and eye-tracking.

developments.title: Won’t it fall off the nose?

sections.text: A microstructured, skin-compatible contact layer integrated into the transparent nose support to enhance grip and reduce slipping without altering the eyewear’s original form.

sections.title: Advantages
sections.text: Reusable adhesion potential, minimal visual impact, improved grip.

sections.title: Limitations
sections.text: Performance under sweat and skin oils requires validation; hygiene and skin comfort must be tested.

developments.title: Why TRACE IV?
developments.text: It represents the explorer discovering the stories hidden within historical artifacts and following the traces left behind from the past to the present.

sections.text: The Roman numeral IV (4) symbolizes the interpretation of time as the fourth dimension.
